title: Liquor rule changes to speed restaurant applications
summary: In July 2026 the vice chair proposed rule changes to ease things for businesses, a restaurant operator said he waits about three weeks for email replies, and the commission voted to rework the application deadline rule and repeal a restroom rule pending a public hearing. In September staff said they would ask corporation counsel about signature and notarization rules on liquor forms.

timeline.text: Staff will ask Corporation Counsel for legal advice on all forms that require notarization.
The next available hearing on that change would be in September.
Commissioners voted to repeal (remove) that sanitation rule and publish the change in the Maui News for a public hearing.
The director said a current rule requires separate men's and women's restrooms for customers.
The commission voted for the same follow-up work on the rules about changing a business's licensed space.
A second motion asked the vice chair to work with the department on a form to streamline trade name (business name) changes.
The application deadline rule will stay on the agenda for next month.
The commission voted to have the vice chair work with the department on new wording for the application deadline rule.
A commissioner suggested putting electronic signatures on next month's agenda.
The Maui Chamber of Commerce testified in support of clear timelines for processing license applications.
A restaurant operator said he sometimes waits about three weeks for an email reply on his application.
The vice chair said her proposed rule changes aim to make things easier for businesses in a tough economy while keeping public safety in mind.
